title: Easy weeknight dinners for fall, plus how long leftovers last
dek: Three simple fall dinners that stretch into tomorrow's lunch, with the USDA's rules for storing and reheating the extras safely.
keyPoints: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour if it is above 90°F.
Cooked leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge or 3 to 4 months in the freezer.
Reheat leftovers to 165°F; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil.
Split big batches into shallow containers so they cool quickly.

sources.title: Leftovers and Food Safety | Food Safety and Inspection Service
How long will cooked food stay safe in the refrigerator?

body: If you are looking for a Tuesday dinner that takes little thought, three dependable options cover most kitchens. A pot of soup built from whatever vegetables are in the fridge. A sheet pan of chicken pieces and cut potatoes roasted together in a hot oven. Pasta with a jar of sauce and a bagged salad on the side. Each one uses a single pot or pan and scales up easily.

Scaling up is the useful part. Cooking a double batch tonight means tomorrow's lunch or Thursday's dinner is already done. Soup and pasta sauce also freeze well, so a big pot can cover a night next week when nobody wants to cook.

Extra food only helps if it is stored safely. The USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service says leftovers should go into the refrigerator within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour if the temperature is above 90°F. Dividing a big pot of soup or a tray of chicken into shallow containers helps it cool to 40°F or below quickly, which keeps bacteria from multiplying.

The agency says refrigerated leftovers are safe for 3 to 4 days, and frozen leftovers keep for 3 to 4 months. When you reheat them, bring them to 165°F on a food thermometer, and heat soups, sauces and gravies to a rolling boil. A strip of masking tape with the date on each container makes the 3 to 4 day rule easy to follow.
Tonight, pick the one meal your household will eat without complaint, double it, and pack the extras into shallow, dated containers before you sit down.
